The temple subsequently fell into disrepair and was revived and converted to the Rinzai school by the monk {{ill|Enni|de|Enni Ben’en|fr|Enni|ja|円爾|pl|Enni Ben’en|ru|Энни Бэнъэн|simple|Enni|vi|Viên Nhĩ Biện Viên|qid=Q739826|lt=Enni}} in 1262 AD. The temple flourished during the {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period}} and was named one of the [[Five Mountain System#The ''Jissetsu''|''Jissetsu'' temples]] in 1343. It is where {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|ar|أشيكاغا تاكا-أوجي|ca|Ashikaga Takauji|cs|Takaudži Ašikaga|de|Ashikaga Takauji|es|Ashikaga Takauji|eu|Ashikaga Takauji|fa|آشیکاگا تاکائوجی|fi|Ashikaga Takauji|fr|Ashikaga Takauji|hak|Ashikaga Takauji|he|אשיקאגה טאקאוג'י|hu|Asikaga Takaudzsi|id|Ashikaga Takauji|it|Ashikaga Takauji|ja|足利尊氏|ko|아시카가 다카우지|mr|अशिकागा तकाउजी|nl|Ashikaga Takauji|pl|Takauji Ashikaga|pt|Ashikaga Takauji|ru|Асикага Такаудзи|simple|Ashikaga Takauji|sr|Ашикага Такауџи|sv|Ashikaga Takauji|th|อาชิกางะ ทากาอูจิ|tr|Ashikaga Takauji|uk|Асікаґа Такаудзі|vi|Ashikaga Takauji|zh|足利尊氏|zh_min_nan|Asikaga Takauzi|zh_yue|足利尊氏|qid=Q297107|lt=Ashikaga Takauji}} and {{ill|Imagawa Yoshimoto|ar|إيماغاوا يوشيموتو|ca|Imagawa Yoshimoto|cs|Jošimoto Imagawa|de|Imagawa Yoshimoto|eo|Imagawa Yoshimoto|es|Imagawa Yoshimoto|fa|ایماگاوا یوشیموتو|fi|Imagawa Yoshimoto|fr|Imagawa Yoshimoto|glk|ایماگاوا یوشیموتو|hu|Imagava Josimoto|id|Imagawa Yoshimoto|it|Imagawa Yoshimoto|ja|今川義元|ko|이마가와 요시모토|ms|Imagawa Yoshimoto|pl|Yoshimoto Imagawa|pt|Imagawa Yoshimoto|ru|Имагава Ёсимото|sk|Jošimoto Imagawa|sr|Имагава Јошимото|th|อิมางาวะ โยชิโมโตะ|tr|Imagawa Yoshimoto|uk|Імаґава Йосімото|vi|Imagawa Yoshimoto|zh|今川義元|zh_min_nan|Imagawa Yosimoto|zh_yue|今川義元|zu|Imagawa Yoshimoto|qid=Q1054305|lt=Imagawa Yoshimoto}} took the tonsure. In the {{ill|Sengoku period|ar|فترة سينغوكو|arz|فتره سينجوكو|be|Перыяд Сэнгоку|bg|Сенгоку|bn|সেনগোকু যুগ|bo|སེན་གོའི་དུས་མཚམས་|ca|Període Sengoku|ckb|سەردەمی سێنگۆکو|cs|Období Sengoku|de|Sengoku-Zeit|eo|Epoko Sengoku|es|Período Sengoku|et|Sengoku ajastu|eu|Sengoku aroa|fa|دوره سنگوکو|fi|Sengoku-kausi|fr|Époque Sengoku|ga|Tréimhse Sengoku|glk|سنگؤکۊ زمات|he|תקופת סנגוקו|hu|Hadakozó fejedelemségek kora (Japán)|id|Zaman Sengoku|is|Sengoku-öldin|it|Periodo Sengoku|ja|戦国時代 (日本)|ka|სენგოკუს პერიოდი|kk|Сэнгоку дәуірі|ko|센고쿠 시대|lt|Sengoku laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Sengoku|nl|Sengokuperiode|no|Sengoku-perioden|pl|Sengoku (okres)|pt|Período Sengoku|ro|Perioada Sengoku|ru|Период Сэнгоку|sh|Sengoku razdoblje|simple|Sengoku period|sk|Obdobie Sengoku|sq|Periudha Sengoku|sr|Сенгоку период|sv|Sengoku|th|ยุคเซ็งโงกุ|tl|Panahong Sengoku|tr|Sengoku Dönemi|uk|Період Сенґоку|ur|سینگوکو دور|uz|Sengoku davri|vi|Thời kỳ Chiến Quốc (Nhật Bản)|wuu|战国时代（日本）|zh|战国时代 (日本)|zh_min_nan|Sengoku sî-tāi|zh_yue|戰國時代 (日本)|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period}}, when the young {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|en|Tokugawa Ieyasu|qid=Q171977|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu}} was held hostage in {{ill|Sunpu Domain|fa|قلمرو سونپو|fr|Domaine de Sunpu|ja|駿府藩|ko|슨푸번|pt|Domínio de Shizuoka|ru|Сидзуока (княжество)|zh|骏府藩|qid=Q3034530|lt=Sunpu}} by the [[Imagawa clan]], he was sent to Seiken-ji to be tutored by the abbot {{ill|Sessai Chōrō|en|Sessai Chōrō|qid=Q842029|lt=Sessai Chōrō}}. During the invasion of {{ill|Suruga Province|en|Suruga Province|qid=Q864170|lt=Suruga Province}} by the [[Takeda clan]], {{ill|Imagawa Ujizane|en|Imagawa Ujizane|qid=Q3100078|lt=Imagawa Ujizane}} established his headquarters at this temple.

During the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Έντο|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, the temple continued to flourish due to its connection with Tokugawa Ieyasu, and its location on the Tōkaidō highway linking {{ill|Edo|en|Edo|qid=Q215646|lt=Edo}} with {{ill|Kyoto|en|Kyoto|qid=Q34600|lt=Kyoto}}. It was selected by the [[Tokugawa shogunate]] as one of the lodging spots for the {{ill|Joseon missions to Japan|en|Joseon missions to Japan|qid=Q15290174|lt=Joseon missions to Japan}} and the delegations from the {{ill|Ryukyu Kingdom|ar|مملكة ريوكيو|ast|Reinu de Ryūkyū|azb|ریوکیو کراللیغی|bar|Kinireich Ryukyu|be|Рукю (дзяржава)|bxr|Люучюу улас|ca|Regne de Ryūkyū|cdo|Liù-giù-guók|cs|Království Rjúkjú|da|Kongeriget Ryukyu|de|Königreich Ryūkyū|eo|Rjukju-reĝlando|es|Reino de Ryūkyū|eu|Ryukyuko Erresuma|fa|پادشاهی ریوکیو|fi|Ryūkyū-kuningaskunta|fr|Royaume de Ryūkyū|gan|琉球國|gl|Reino de Ryukyu|hak|Liù-khiù-koet|haw|Aupuni Mōʻī o Liu Kiu|hu|Rjúkjúi Királyság|id|Kerajaan Ryukyu|it|Regno delle Ryūkyū|ja|琉球王国|km|អាណាចក្ររីយូឃ្យូ|ko|류큐국|lo|ອານາຈັກຣີວກີວ|lt|Riukiu karalystė|mn|Рюүкюү улс|ms|Kerajaan Ryukyu|nl|Koninkrijk Riukiu|no|Kongedømmet Ryukyu|pl|Królestwo Riukiu|pnb|ریؤکیؤ بادشاہت|pt|Reino de Ryukyu|ru|Рюкю (государство)|sco|Ryukyu Kinrick|simple|Ryukyu Kingdom|sv|Kungariket Ryukyu|th|อาณาจักรรีวกีว|tl|Kaharian ng Ryukyu|tr|Ryukyu Krallığı|uk|Королівство Рюкю|ur|مملکت ریوکیو|vi|Vương quốc Lưu Cầu|wuu|琉球国|za|Liuzgiuzgoz|zh|琉球国|zh_classical|琉球國|zh_min_nan|Liû-kiû-kok|zh_yue|琉球國|qid=Q28025|lt=Ryukyu Kingdom}}.  Due to these connections it was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1994.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/206953 |title=朝鮮通信使遺跡|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}}</ref> Surviving Edo period structures include the ''[[Sanmon]]'' (1651) and entrance to the {{ill|Main Hall (Japanese Buddhism)|en|Main Hall (Japanese Buddhism)|qid=Q17051413|lt=Main Hall}} (1616).<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>

During the early {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}, the tracks of the {{ill|Tōkaidō Main Line|en|Tōkaidō Main Line|qid=Q1190152|lt=Tōkaidō Main Line}} railway were laid across the front of the temple, which lost much of its properties. However, due to its scenic location overlooking {{ill|Suruga Bay|en|Suruga Bay|qid=Q1201023|lt=Suruga Bay}}, the temple drew the attention of poets and writers, including [[:en:Shimazaki Tōson|Shimazaki Tōson]], {{ill|Takayama Chogyū|en|Takayama Chogyū|qid=Q461853|lt=Takayama Chogyū}} and {{ill|Natsume Sōseki|en|Natsume Sōseki|qid=Q180903|lt=Natsume Sōseki}}.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

The temple was also the location of an important conference held by the leadership of the fledgling {{ill|Imperial Japanese Navy|en|Imperial Japanese Navy|qid=Q219712|lt=Imperial Japanese Navy}} in June 1887, with the participants discussing various tactics and {{ill|Naval strategy|en|Naval strategy|qid=Q11559269|lt=fleet maneuvers}}, which would then be tested in practice by the fleet in nearby Shimizu harbor.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Evans |first1=David C |last2=Peatty |first2=Mark |title=Kaigun: Strategy, Tactics, and Technology in the Imperial Japanese Navy, 1887-1941 |date=2012 |publisher=Naval Institute Press |isbn=978-1591142447 |pages=35–36}}</ref>

==Cultural properties==

===National Important Cultural Properties===
====Diary of Ye Mengde====
Diary of '''Ye Mengde''' ({{zh|t=葉夢得|w='''Yeh Meng-te'''}}; 1077–1148), a {{ill|Song dynasty|en|Song dynasty|qid=Q7462|lt=Song dynasty}} Chinese scholar, poet, and government minister, dated summer of 1149 AD<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/156808|title=宋版石林先生尚書伝 自巻第一至第四 紹興二十九年仲夏刊記|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}}</ref>

===National Place of Scenic Beauty===
==== Seiken-ji gardens====
The {{ill|Japanese garden|en|Japanese garden|qid=Q15835|lt=Japanese garden}} at Seiken-ji dates from the early Edo period and contains ponds and tree arrangements. It became a nationally designated [[Monuments of Japan|Place of Scenic Beauty]] in 1936.<ref name="Bunka2">{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/162831|title=清見寺庭園|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=}}</ref>
